root_cause: The Escape key's cancel event becomes non-cancelable after successive backdrop transitions, causing preventDefault() to have no effect and the dialog to close despite keyboard:false.
repair_strategy: Modify the Escape keydown listener in dialog-base.ts to also handle modal dialogs when keyboard:false by preventing default and returning early, thus suppressing the cancel event before it fires.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will no longer dismiss the dialog, allowing users to remain focused on the OTP input and complete the transfer via explicit Cancel or Send actions, satisfying the requirement that the dialog stays open until an explicit user action.
functional_risks: Potential interference with Escape usage in non-modal dialogs when keyboard:true, but the guard preserves existing behavior.
Risk is low because the change only affects modal dialogs with keyboard:false and mirrors the existing cancel listener logic.
verification_requirements: Confirm that pressing Escape any number of times does not close the dialog when opened with { keyboard: false, backdrop: 'static' }.
Confirm that pressing Escape still closes the dialog when opened with keyboard:true (modal) or for non-modal dialogs.
Ensure the Cancel and Send buttons continue to function as expected.
Verify focus remains on the OTP input after Escape presses until an explicit action is taken.
